text:
William Nylander is in the middle of Toronto's storm: trade speculation, a four-game skid, and his own line to TSN that it's "not that slumpy." On the scoresheet he's right: 11 goals and 22 points in 20 games is exactly the Nylander pace.

Underneath, though, the Leafs are getting crushed with him on the ice: 39% of the expected goals at five on five, more than ten points worse than without him. His finishing (20%) is near his usual standard, so the goals are mostly real, but Toronto has scored about four more than expected with him out there and his last ten games have come in under what his chances would predict. Daily Faceoff Toronto reported he's focused on his play away from the puck, which fits: Evolving-Hockey had opponents' chances rising with him on last season (bottom 6% of forwards).

He's a transition player (60% of his shots off the rush, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) on a team that hasn't had the puck. Our range: 78 to 106 points.
